ECG Machine.name: Printing problem
causes: Printer paper may be empty or incorrectly loaded.
The printer status or connection may need checking.
A device or software setting may be preventing printing.
checks: Check paper supply and loading according to the manufacturer instructions.
Check the visible printer/status indicators and approved connections.
Retry the operation according to the device SOP.
If the problem persists, escalate to qualified biomedical/technical personnel.
ECG Machine.safety: Do not open the equipment enclosure or perform internal electrical repairs. Follow hospital SOP and manufacturer instructions.

ECG Machine.name: Noisy or abnormal ECG trace
causes: Electrode contact may be poor.
A lead may be loose or incorrectly connected.
Patient movement or electrical interference may affect the trace.
checks: Check electrode placement and skin contact.
Check lead connections and visible cable condition.
Reduce avoidable movement/interference according to the clinical procedure.
ECG Machine.safety: Do not rely on a malfunctioning signal for clinical decisions. Escalate persistent faults.

Patient Monitor.name: SpO2 reading problem
causes: Sensor placement or contact may be poor.
The sensor or cable may be damaged.
Patient movement may affect the measurement.
checks: Check sensor placement and cable connection.
Check the sensor for visible damage.
Follow the monitor's instructions for an appropriate measurement site.
Patient Monitor.safety: Monitor readings require appropriate clinical interpretation. Escalate persistent equipment faults.

Patient Monitor.name: ECG/lead problem
causes: ECG electrodes or leads may have poor contact.
A lead may be disconnected.
Motion or electrical interference may affect the trace.
checks: Check lead connections and electrode contact.
Check visible cable condition.
Follow the manufacturer's monitoring procedure.
Patient Monitor.safety: Do not rely on a malfunctioning monitor for patient care. Escalate faults according to hospital procedure.

Infusion Pump.name: Occlusion or pressure alarm
causes: The infusion line may be kinked or obstructed.
Tubing may not be correctly positioned.
The device may be detecting abnormal downstream pressure.
checks: Check the tubing for visible kinks or obstruction.
Check tubing placement according to the pump instructions.
Follow the hospital protocol for responding to infusion alarms.
Infusion Pump.safety: Do not bypass alarms or alter infusion settings without appropriate authorization. Escalate persistent faults.

Infusion Pump.name: Power or battery problem
causes: The power source may be unavailable.
The battery may be depleted.
The power connection may not be secure.
checks: Check the approved power connection.
Check the battery/status indicator.
Follow the manufacturer's procedure for power and battery checks.
Infusion Pump.safety: Do not open the pump for internal repair. Remove from clinical use and escalate if safe operation cannot be confirmed.

Ventilator.name: Flow or expiratory sensor problem
causes: The flow sensor may be disconnected or incorrectly positioned.
The breathing circuit may have a connection or obstruction issue.
The sensor may require inspection according to the manufacturer procedure.
checks: Check visible circuit connections.
Check sensor connection and placement according to device instructions.
Follow the ventilator alarm and troubleshooting procedure.
Ventilator.safety: Ventilator faults can directly affect patient safety. Do not improvise repairs; follow emergency clinical procedures and contact qualified personnel.

Ventilator.name: High-pressure or alarm condition
causes: The breathing circuit may be kinked or obstructed.
The alarm may indicate a device or patient-related condition.
A clinical assessment may be required.
checks: Check visible circuit connections and tubing.
Follow the ventilator alarm procedure.
Ensure appropriate clinical staff assess the patient and situation.
Ventilator.safety: Never bypass an alarm without addressing its cause and following the clinical protocol.

Defibrillator.name: Power or battery problem
causes: The battery may be depleted.
The approved power connection may not be available.
A device fault may be present.
checks: Check device power/battery indicators.
Check the approved power connection.
Confirm required status/self-test indicators according to manufacturer instructions.
Defibrillator.safety: Defibrillators are critical emergency devices. Do not open or internally repair them; follow emergency equipment procedures.

Defibrillator.name: Pad/electrode connection problem
causes: Pads/electrodes may not be correctly connected.
Consumables may be expired or unavailable.
The device may report a technical fault.
checks: Check visible connections and consumable status.
Check the displayed fault/status message.
Follow the manufacturer's procedure and hospital emergency protocol.
Defibrillator.safety: Do not test or deliver therapy to a person as part of troubleshooting. Use approved test procedures and qualified personnel.

Hemodialysis Machine.name: Alarm condition
causes: The machine may be detecting a pressure, conductivity, or temperature condition.
A connection or consumable condition may need checking.
The alarm may require the manufacturer's specific procedure.
checks: Read the displayed alarm message carefully.
Check only visible connections and consumables permitted by the SOP.
Follow the manufacturer's alarm procedure and escalate when required.
Hemodialysis Machine.safety: Dialysis equipment is life-supporting therapy equipment. Do not bypass alarms or perform internal repair without qualified authorization.

Suction Machine.name: Low or no suction
causes: The tubing or collection system may be disconnected or obstructed.
The collection container may be full or incorrectly assembled.
The filter or tubing condition may need checking.
checks: Check visible tubing connections and the collection container.
Check for visible obstruction according to the device instructions.
Follow the manufacturer's procedure for filter/container checks.
Suction Machine.safety: Do not open internal components while connected to power. Escalate persistent faults.
